Hotel 77

Every bedroom in a hotel that loops

  • RoleLevel Designer · Game Developer
  • TeamFewer than 10
  • TimelineContract project
  • StatusUnreleased — Steam page live, wishlist open
  • Built withUnity · C#
Wishlist on Steam

The project

A first-person narrative horror game set in a haunted hotel caught in a temporal loop: you play a reporter investigating Hotel 77 in Arkham, Massachusetts on 7 July 1997, navigating repeating corridors, identifying anomalies and making the right call to move time forward. I designed and developed several of the anomalies, the letter, every one of the hotel's bedrooms, the audio logs and the lore, cut the trailers, and helped fix bugs. The Steam page is live and localized into ten languages with full English audio; the game has not released yet.

What I owned

  • Several of the anomalies, designed and implemented
  • Every bedroom in the hotel
  • The letter, the audio logs and the lore
  • Trailers
  • Bug fixing across the project

A problem I solved

My job on this was level design. But building and testing rooms all day means you walk into bugs constantly — far more of them than someone reviewing a build for half an hour ever will.

I could have filed them and moved on; that was within my remit. Instead I volunteered to help fix them, which meant working outside the role I was hired for on a small team where nobody had spare capacity. On a team of fewer than ten, the useful thing to be is the person who closes the issue rather than the person who reports it.

Result

A hotel whose bedrooms, letter, audio logs and lore I own, plus a meaningfully shorter bug list than the one I found. It is heading to Steam in ten languages.

What I'd do differently

Come back with the experience I have now and design more interesting anomalies. The anomaly *is* the game here, and I know more about making one land than I did in 2024.
